summary.plain: DM32 was an early dark matter search with three sodium iodide crystals (32 kg) run by a Zaragoza group in the Canfranc underground laboratory, Spain, from 1993 to 1994. It set competitive limits and looked for a yearly modulation.
summary.technical: Three 10.7 kg NaI(Tl) modules (32.1 kg in all), originally an active veto of a germanium double-beta experiment, at Canfranc; 4613.6 kg d of data (May 1993 - December 1994) analysed for an excess in the total rate and for annual modulation; competitive spin-independent and spin-dependent limits, with the modulation analysis improving the excluded parameter space by about two orders of magnitude (per the 2026 review).

technology.quote: The experiment consisted of three 10.7 kg NaI(Tl) modules with a total mass of 32.1 kg.
